title: NER span adjudication: legacy offsets, voting, overlaps
scenario: Annotator NER spans from two tools (legacy: 1-based inclusive; v2: 0-based exclusive) are converted, trimmed, voted on (2 distinct annotators needed), and overlap-resolved by votes then length. Test 2 checks summary counts.

verified.why_correct: `text[end - 1]` looks like an off-by-one, but end is exclusive, so the last character of the span is at end - 1. Both loops stop when start meets end, so an all-whitespace span collapses to empty and is dropped by make_span.

bugs.title: Legacy end shifted as if it were 1-based exclusive
bugs.symptom: test_1_adjudication.test_legacy_tool_offsets: D04 comes out as [[13, 17, 'LOC', 'Pari'], [37, 43, 'DATE', '12 Jun']]; every legacy span is one character short and Lima is missing.
bugs.why: A 1-based inclusive end is numerically the same as a 0-based exclusive end, so only start needs shifting. Subtracting 1 from end too cuts the last character off every legacy span (Paris -> Pari), which also breaks agreement with the v2 annotator.
hints: Every D04 entity is one character short. Which tool produced D04's spans?
Work the README's Paris example through to_zero_based by hand.
Only start moves: return start - 1, end.
probes: Why did Lima disappear entirely instead of just losing a character?
Why is a 1-based inclusive end equal to a 0-based exclusive end?

bugs.title: Equal-vote overlaps not ranked by length
bugs.old: for ent in sorted(entities, key=lambda e: (-e.votes, -e.length, e.start)):
bugs.new: for ent in sorted(entities, key=lambda e: (-e.votes, e.start)):
bugs.symptom: test_1_adjudication.test_overlapping_spans: D02's first entity is [4, 10, 'PER', 'Morgan'] instead of [4, 18, 'ORG', 'Morgan Stanley'].
bugs.why: Morgan Stanley (ORG) and Morgan (PER) both have 2 votes and the same start. Without the length key the stable sort keeps the candidates' offset order, where the shorter span comes first, so PER 'Morgan' is kept.
hints: D02 keeps 'Morgan' as PER. How many votes did each overlapping candidate get?
Look at the ranking key in resolve_doc against the README overlap rule.
Add -e.length between votes and start in the sort key.
probes: Why did the shorter span win rather than an arbitrary one?
Why didn't named_entities change even though the label did?

bugs.title: `== "PER" or "ORG"` counts every entity
bugs.why: `ent[2] == "PER" or "ORG"` parses as `(ent[2] == "PER") or "ORG"`, and the non-empty string is always truthy, so LOC and DATE entities are counted too.
hints: named_entities equals the total entity count. Is that plausible?
Look at the condition in the named_entities sum.
Compare against both labels: ent[2] in ("PER", "ORG").
probes: How does Python group `a == b or c`?
Why didn't any Test 1 assertion notice?

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_report()?
context_qa.a: `load_docs` builds doc_id -> text, `read_spans` turns spans.csv rows into cleaned Span objects, `candidates` groups them by (doc, start, end, label) and keeps groups with at least MIN_VOTES distinct annotators, then `resolve_doc` picks the non-overlapping entities for each doc. The summary is computed from the resolved entities.

Rows whose doc id (trimmed, upper-cased) is not in docs.json, rows where start or end isn't an integer, and anything for which make_span returns None (bad label, out-of-bounds offsets, empty after trimming).

context_qa.q: What does to_zero_based return for each tool?
context_qa.a: For `legacy` it returns a shifted `(start, end)` pair computed in its `if` branch; for any other tool it returns the inputs unchanged.

context_qa.q: How are votes counted in candidates()?
context_qa.a: A dict keyed by (doc_id, start, end, label) holds a set of annotator ids, so repeat marks by the same (lower-cased) annotator count once. Groups are iterated in sorted key order, so each doc's candidate list is in (start, end, label) order.
`_overlaps(a, b)` is `a.start < b.end and b.start < a.end` on exclusive ends, so spans that only touch (one ends where the other starts) do not overlap.

context_qa.q: What does the annotators field count?
context_qa.a: The number of distinct lower-cased annotator ids among the spans returned by read_spans, i.e. after cleaning but before voting.
